questions.question: Champaran Satyagraha was launched in which of the following years?
questions.solution:
• Champaran Satyagraha: 1917
  • Fact: This was Gandhi's first Satyagraha in India, launched to support indigo farmers against the exploitative 'Tinkathia' system.

questions.question: Swami Vivekananda established Ramakrishna Mission in the year ______.
questions.solution:
• Ramakrishna Mission: 1897
  • Detail: Swami Vivekananda founded the mission at Belur Math to promote the teachings of his guru, Ramakrishna Paramhansa, and social service.

questions.question: Which Mughal emperor built the city called 'Makhsudabad' later popularly known as Murshidabad?
questions.solution:
• Murshidabad Origin: Akbar
  • History: Akbar originally built the town as Makhsudabad; it was later renamed Murshidabad by Murshid Quli Khan when he shifted the capital of Bengal there.

questions.question: Who among the following was NOT a ruler of the Kushana dynasty?
questions.solution:
• Kushana Dynasty: Nahapana
  • Correction: Nahapana was a prominent ruler of the Western Kshatrapas (Sakas), not the Kushanas. Huvishka, Vasudeva, and Vasishka were Kushana kings.

questions.question: ______ was the Mughal emperor during the revolt of 1857.
questions.solution:
• 1857 Emperor: Bahadur Shah II
  • Fact: Also known as Bahadur Shah Zafar, he was the last Mughal emperor and was declared the symbolic leader of the 1857 revolt.

questions.question: The second Round Table Conference was held in 1931 in which of the following countries?
questions.solution:
• Round Table Conference: The UK
  • 1931: The Second RTC was held in London; it was the only conference attended by Mahatma Gandhi as the representative of the INC.

questions.question: Who among the following sultans of the Delhi Sultanate appointed Ghiyasuddin Balban as his/her Prime Minister?
questions.solution:
• Balban's Appointment: Nasiruddin Mahmud
  • Context: Balban served as the powerful Naib (deputy) and Prime Minister under Sultan Nasiruddin Mahmud before eventually ascending the throne himself.

questions.question: In which of the following years was the Diwani of Bengal transferred to the East India Company?
questions.solution:
• Diwani of Bengal: 1765
  • Treaty: Following the Battle of Buxar, the Treaty of Allahabad granted the British East India Company the right to collect revenues (Diwani) from Bengal, Bihar, and Odisha.

questions.question: Who among the following was a leader who led a revolt against the British rule from North East India?
questions.solution:
• NE Revolt Leader: Rani Gaidinliu
  • Title: Known as the 'Rani of the Nagas,' she led a spiritual and political movement against British rule in Manipur and surrounding areas.

questions.question: Prabhavati Gupta, the Queen Regent of the Vakataka empire, was the daughter of Kuberanaga and ______.
questions.solution:
• Prabhavati Gupta: Chandragupta II
  • Lineage: She was the daughter of the Gupta Emperor Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya) and played a key role as Queen Regent of the Vakatakas.

questions.question: What was the outcome of the Gandhi-Irwin Pact of 1931?
questions.option_2: Indian National Congress agreed to end the Civil Disobedience Movement.
questions.option_3: Indian National Congress agreed on a peaceful partition of Bengal.
questions.option_4: Bhagat Singh, Rajguru and Sukhdev were to be given a fair trial.
questions.solution:
• 1931 Pact Outcome: INC agreed to end the Civil Disobedience Movement
  • Detail: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact led to the release of political prisoners and the participation of the Congress in the Second Round Table Conference.

questions.question: Which monument was built in 1924 to welcome King George V and Queen Mary?
questions.solution:
• Gateway of India: 1924
  • Architecture: Built in Mumbai, it was designed by George Wittet to commemorate the 1911 visit of King George V and Queen Mary.

questions.question: Who among the following was appointed as the curator of ancient monuments in year 1880?
questions.solution:
• Monuments Curator: HH Cole
  • 1880: Major H.H. Cole was appointed as the first Curator of Ancient Monuments in India, focusing on conservation before the formal ASI expansion.

questions.question: Which of the following dynasties made Kanauj (Kanyakubja) its capital city?
questions.solution:
• Kannauj Capital: Pratihara dynasty
  • Power Shift: The Gurjara-Pratiharas successfully controlled Kannauj during the Tripartite Struggle, making it their primary political center.

questions.question: Identify the revolutionary from West Bengal who participated in the freedom movement.
questions.solution:
• Bengal Revolutionary: Khudiram Bose
  • Fact: One of the youngest revolutionaries, he was executed at age 18 for the Muzaffarpur conspiracy (attempted assassination of Kingsford).

questions.question: In which year did the East-India Company acquire the Diwani of Bengal?
questions.solution:
• Diwani Acquisition: 1765
  • Mughal Grant: Emperor Shah Alam II granted the Diwani rights to the Company, which transformed it from a trading body to a ruling power.

questions.question: Which one of the following was the last imperial dynasty to rule China?
questions.solution:
• Last Chinese Dynasty: Qing dynasty
  • History: The Qing (Manchu) dynasty ruled from 1644 until the Xinhai Revolution of 1912, when China became a republic.

questions.question: The Lucknow Pact of December 1916 was an understanding between the Indian National Congress and the ______.
questions.solution:
• Lucknow Pact: Muslim League
  • 1916: This pact was a historic agreement between the INC and the Muslim League to pressure the British for self-government and communal representation.

questions.question: Fort Saint Louis was a ______ fort that stood in Pondicherry on the eastern coast of India.
questions.solution:
• Fort Saint Louis: French
  • Colonialism: This was a strategic French fortification in Pondicherry, their main headquarters on the Coromandel Coast.

questions.question: Which of the following empires was founded by Harihara and Bukka in 1336?
questions.solution:
• Vijayanagara Empire: Vijayanagara empire
  • Founders: Brothers Harihara and Bukka established this South Indian empire on the banks of the Tungabhadra River to resist northern invasions.

questions.question: In the context of Mughal administration, which of the following is the most appropriate definition of 'Abwab'?
questions.option_1: A clerk in the government treasury
questions.option_2: A tax levied on the lands over and above the original rent
questions.solution:
• Abwab Definition: A tax levied on the lands over and above the original rent
  • Mughal Admin: Abwabs were miscellaneous cesses or additional taxes imposed by the government or zamindars.

questions.question: The Chalukya dynasty was a major kingdom in the ______ part of India.
questions.solution:
• Chalukya Location: southern
  • Fact: The Chalukyas of Badami were a dominant power in the Deccan and Southern India between the 6th and 12th centuries.

questions.question: Who among the following rulers inscribed his messages to his subjects and officials on stone surfaces?
questions.solution:
• Edicts of Ashoka: Ashoka
  • Propaganda: Emperor Ashoka was the first Indian ruler to use rock and pillar inscriptions to communicate his principles of Dhamma directly to the public.

questions.question: In which of the following years was the Supreme Court set up in Calcutta by the East India Company?
questions.solution:
• Supreme Court: 1773
  • Legislation: The Regulating Act of 1773 led to the establishment of the Supreme Court of Judicature at Fort William, Calcutta.

questions.question: Who among the following Sikh Gurus laid the foundation of ‘Khalsa Panth’?
questions.solution:
• Khalsa Panth: Guru Gobind Singh
  • 1699: The tenth Sikh Guru, Guru Gobind Singh, created the Khalsa (the Pure) to provide a military and spiritual identity to Sikhs.
